notes: Its people intentionally abandoned conventional magic.
Its culture centers on folklore, cryptids, fairy tales, and fragmented glimpses of the wider world.
Magically gifted visitors would likely be revered rather than feared.
Its people reject formal magic but unknowingly preserve it through folklore, fairy tales, legends, and cryptids.
Visitors who openly use magic may be viewed as witches or deities.
Strange occurrences from other realms become local myths.
Ciri becomes the official keeper of Lith's keystone.
Lith publicly rejects magic, treating it as folklore, fairy tales, and cryptids despite genuine magic existing there.
Occasional planar gaps allow creatures from other realms to appear, becoming the basis of local legends.
